children.topic: Pancreatic Head Adenocarcinoma
Origin / Key Risk Factor: Chronic pancreatitis & Smoking
Key Clinical Sign / Triad: Malignant Obstructive Jaundice, Courvoisier’s Law (Palpable non-tender GB)
Diagnostic / Staging Gold Standard: Triple-Phase Contrast CT (Do NOT perform routine pre-op biopsy or stenting)
Surgical Treatment of Choice: Whipple’s Procedure (Delayed gastric emptying is the #1 complication)
Ampullary Carcinoma
Origin / Key Risk Factor: Periampullary tissue
Key Clinical Sign / Triad: Fluctuating jaundice (remits due to sloughing/necrosis)
Diagnostic / Staging Gold Standard: ERCP with direct tumor biopsy
Surgical Treatment of Choice: Whipple’s Procedure (Carries an excellent prognosis)
Insulinoma
Origin / Key Risk Factor: Pancreatic Beta Cells
Key Clinical Sign / Triad: Whipple's Triad (Hypoglycemia + neuro symptoms + glucose relief)
Diagnostic / Staging Gold Standard: Fasting hypoglycemia + elevated C-peptide (>25), Intra-op High-Res U/S (most accurate)
Surgical Treatment of Choice: Enucleation (if benign & solitary)
Gastrinoma (Zollinger-Ellison)
Origin / Key Risk Factor: Non-Beta Cells in Gastrinoma Triangle
Key Clinical Sign / Triad: Refractory peptic ulcers & secretory diarrhea
Diagnostic / Staging Gold Standard: Fasting Gastrin > 1,000 pg/mL & gastric pH < 2.5
Surgical Treatment of Choice: Duodenal/Pancreatic Enucleation or Whipple (based on size/location)
